summary: Quick console walkthrough focused on per-route dashboards, usage analytics, and actionable cost breakdowns. LumenX is evaluating Redwood to reduce per-token costs across chat and reranking routes and to get clearer team-level allocation for billing. Demo showed route filters, token-level cost waterfall, Optimize suggestions (batching, kv caching, quant profiles), and how to export cost-attribution reports. Customer asked about SSO/SAML, data retention, and pilot pricing; Redwood team agreed to share dashboard link, sample export, and pricing scenarios. Next: pilot kickoff and logs for Optimize assessment.
notes: Call recorded via Fireflies; some words auto-transcribed incorrectly (route names, model ids). Multiple references to Optimize heuristic suggestions and cost vs latency tradeoffs. Customer interested in per-team chargebacks and anomaly detection on route cost spikes.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Rivera: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex from Redwood, AE on the account. We got Priya from our SE team and Jonah for the console walkthrough. Can you hear me ok?
[00:06] Tom Ng: Yeah, loud and clear. Thanks Alex. We wanted to see the console and specifically per-route cost stuff — we've got chat routes and a separate reranker and our FinOps lead Sofia is on to see allocation.
[00:15] Priya Shah: Great, thanks Tom. Quick agenda: I'm gonna show the Console -> Routes page, how we break down tokens and cost per route, the token-level waterfall, then a quick run through Optimize suggestions for batching and quant settings, and finally exports and alerts.
[00:27] Sofia Ruiz: Perfect. We care about being able to show each product team their billable units per month and detect when a route spikes unexpectedly.
[00:34] Jonah Kim: Also will hit how routing policies affect cost — e.g., fallbacks to cheaper model variants during heavy traffic.
[00:40] Maya Patel: One ask: we use a lot of short chat turns but also long system prompts; curious how that mixes into the waterfall.
[00:47] Priya Shah: Good question; we'll show token distribution and the sample breakdown — prompt, response, system tokens, and KV cache hits if applicable.

[01:02] [00:60] Priya Shah: Opening the Console now... ok clicking Routes. You should see LumenX org, then filter for project "search-and-chat" — note the auto-suggestion for tags.
[01:12] Tom Ng: I see it, nice. The list shows route names, approximate 24h cost estimates, and a colored sparkline.
[01:18] Priya Shah: Exactly. Click into "chat-main-prod" — this is our typical Chat route. Once inside, top-right you can change time window, group by tag, and compare against last period.
[01:29] [01:30] Priya Shah: Scrolling down — we have the token waterfall: request prompt tokens, system tokens, response tokens, kv-cache saved tokens, and execution overhead. Each band ties to cost. Notice the per-token unit price is pulled from your plan; for hosted it's X per 1k, for dedicated it's based on committed capacity.
[01:45] Sofia Ruiz: That waterfall is great. Can we attribute to team tags?
[01:48] Priya Shah: Yes, use the tag filter at top. If routes include "team:search" or if SDK calls set folder/project metadata, we roll that into the attribution. You can export a CSV by clicking the export icon — that CSV includes token counts and inferred cost per team.
[01:58] Maya Patel: Are the KV cache hits measured in real time? We rely on prefix caching to reduce cost for long conversations.
[02:03] Priya Shah: We estimate KV cache hit rate from runtime logs; the Console shows observed KV hit ratio and the estimated token savings. Note this is an approximation if you have private on-prem logs — for Private deployments we can integrate runtime telemetry to get exact numbers.

[02:20] [02:20] Jonah Kim: Quick detour — Sofia asked about anomaly detection. We have per-route alerting that can trigger on sudden cost per-minute increases or token-rate spikes, and you can hook that to PagerDuty or Slack.
[02:32] Sofia Ruiz: Important for us. We had one bot regression last quarter where a front-end change caused repeated prompts.
[02:37] Priya Shah: You can configure a rolling baseline and set a threshold; the Console also suggests baselines using seasonality.

[02:50] [02:50] Priya Shah: Now switching to Optimize tab. This is where we run heuristics against your route patterns. For your chat-main-prod route, Optimize suggests: increase batching to 30ms from 10ms for burst workloads, enable prefix KV caching for repeated system prompts, and try 8-bit quantization for the reranker route.
[03:08] Maya Patel: Wait, 8-bit quant for reranker — will that impact MRR reranking accuracy?
[03:12] Priya Shah: Good callout. The Optimize suggestion includes an estimated quality delta with a confidence band. For reranking we estimate a 0.6–1.4% nDCG change at 8-bit; the Console links to model-specific evals. You can also run a canary rollout: 5% traffic to quantized variant and track eval metrics.
[03:28] Tom Ng: Can you show the per-route cost projection if we applied these suggestions?
[03:31] Priya Shah: Sure — toggle the "Apply Optimize suggestions (estimate)" switch and we re-run the cost model for the selected window. Give it a sec... ok. You can see estimated savings: 18% on chat-main-prod and 42% on reranker due to batching + quant. These are estimates based on your sample logs.
[03:50] Sofia Ruiz: Those numbers would be huge. Does the projection include potential increase in latency?
[03:54] Priya Shah: The projection has both cost and latency columns; for chat batching we show median latency increase estimates (in ms) and also P95. For the chat route here, median changes are negligible but P95 goes up by ~30ms in the simulated window.

[04:10] [04:10] Speaker 1 (auto-transcribed): um yeah there's like a — *crosstalk* — so can we export the scenario?
[04:14] Alex Rivera: Yes, you can export the scenario as a CSV or save it as a "savings playbook" to attach to a ticket. We'll share the sample export after the call.

[04:28] [04:30] Priya Shah: Also note per-route SLA badges — if a route is on Dedicated, the Console shows SLA attainment and backpressure behavior. For hosted routes we show fallback models; the routing policy indicates if we switch to cheaper variants when capacity thresholds hit.
[04:45] Maya Patel: On the topic of dedicated vs hosted — if we commit to Dedicated for the reranker, how do we model cost? Is it flat monthly plus per-token?
[04:53] Jonah Kim: Generally Dedicated is committed capacity with a monthly fee; you get lower per-token execution cost within that pool. We model a break-even by comparing your monthly token consumption against the committed pool cost; I'll include a spreadsheet scenario.

[05:10] [05:10] Tom Ng: Security quick checks — SSO, audit logs, KMS.
[05:14] Alex Rivera: We support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and role-based access in the Console. All token-level calls are logged; audit export is available for 13 months by default on enterprise plans, and we have a Private deployment with customer-managed KMS if you need an HSM.
[05:27] Sofia Ruiz: Retention: we need 90-day raw request retention for billing reconciliation.
[05:31] Priya Shah: We can configure retention on Dedicated/Private. For hosted, standard retention is 30 days but enterprise customers can extend with an add-on. We'll capture this as an action item.

[05:48] [05:48] Maya Patel: A small thing — our SDK sets metadata but some older clients don't. Can we retroactively tag traffic for a window?
[05:54] Priya Shah: You can apply corrections in exports: map routes to teams in the CSV. For future real-time attribution, we recommend SDK upgrades or a middleware that injects tags. The Console also allows a manual mapping table for historical reports.

[06:05] [06:05] Priya Shah: Let's demo an export quickly. Click Export -> Cost Attribution -> choose window -> CSV. Opened the sample CSV — you get columns: timestamp, route, project_tag, prompt_tokens, response_tokens, kv_savings_estimate, unit_price, cost_usd.
[06:21] Sofia Ruiz: Can we get that as a S3 drop or push to a BI connector?
[06:25] Priya Shah: Yes, we support scheduled exports to S3 and a BigQuery push for enterprise accounts. We'll include the export config docs link.

[06:38] [06:38] Tom Ng: A question on alerts: can we have an alert when cost for a specific route exceeds a percentage of the monthly budget?
[06:44] Jonah Kim: Yes — create a budget alert and scope it to route tag or project. The alert engine supports percent-of-budget and absolute thresholds and can do composite conditions.

[06:58] [06:58] Maya Patel: If we want to run a pilot, what do you need from our side?
[07:02] Alex Rivera: Two things: sample logs for two weeks (anonymized is fine) so Optimize can run suggestions against your real distribution, and a list of routes you want in the pilot with owners. We will provision a sandbox Console view for LumenX with saved dashboards.
[07:16] Sofia Ruiz: What about pricing for the sandbox?
[07:19] Alex Rivera: Sandbox is free for the pilot. Production pricing options we'll send in the scenario doc.

[07:29] [07:30] Speaker 2 (auto): there's a note about model variants — how do we control fallback grace?
[07:33] Priya Shah: You can set routing policies per route: strict (no fallback), soft (fallback after X% latency degradation), or cost-first (fallback to cheaper variant under high utilization). We showed a sample policy earlier in the Dashboard panel.

[07:48] [07:48] Tom Ng: One more thing: can you show how we track billing for multi-tenant apps? We have multiple customers on a single route.
[07:55] Priya Shah: We recommend per-tenant metadata in SDK calls; if not possible, use session-level tags or proxied headers. The Console will aggregate and allow you to slice by the tenant header if present. For chargeback, you'll need an attribution key; we can show a sample mapping table.

[08:10] [08:10] Priya Shah: Wrapping up demo bits — quick recap: routes -> token waterfall -> tag-based attribution -> Optimize suggestions and projected savings -> exports and alerts -> routing policies and SLA info.
[08:22] Alex Rivera: Ok let's go through next steps and owners. Priya will send the saved dashboard link and a sample export (ACTION). Alex will send pricing scenarios and a pilot OKR template. Maya will upload two weeks of anonymized route logs. We'll schedule pilot kickoff for 10/27.

[08:41] [08:41] Tom Ng: Thanks all, this was helpful — I think Sofia will be excited about the projected savings.
[08:45] Sofia Ruiz: Yeah, lots to digest. We'll follow up internally and get the logs to you.
[08:49] Alex Rivera: Great. We'll follow up via email with links and next steps. Thanks everyone.
[08:54] [08:54] End of recording
